messages.author: e1b933a0d5bbe14f
messages.subject: Complicated regular expression query
parts:
Hi all. I've been wrestling with this issue between projects for a while now with limited success and am hoping I can get some help here. It's an attempted expansion of Stefan's code for concordancing in the book. In that code, if a single corpus line has multiple hits (for example, GREPing for 'the' when many sentences have more than one 'the's), that line gets spread out over multiple columns. This isn't disastrous and there are work-arounds, but I'm trying to do it automatically in R rather than manually in the spreadsheet.

Basically, there are two steps, and I'm stuck on the second. The first is that if the search node appears, say, four time in a line, then the sentence appears in the concordance file four times. This means it has to be duplicated three times. The second step is that, as we don't want all the search nodes surrounded by tabs, each of the duplicated lines has a different instance of the search token tabbed. This is regular expression hell.

The first part isn't *too* hard, but feel free to suggest improvements. I stopped looking when I got it to work and moved on to the next step.

# make and tab simple corpus
corpus<-c('now is the time','the game is the game','i think the movie was the planet of the apes')
node<-'the';node<-paste('\\b',node,'\\b',sep='')
corpus<-gsub(node,'\tthe\t',corpus)

# locate lines with multiple hits
x<-sapply(gregexpr('\t',corpus),length) #gets count of \t per line
has.more.than.1<-which(x>2) #which ones have more than 1 search tokens (or: as each token has 2 tabs, which lines have more than 2)
multiples<-corpus[has.more.than.1] #get just those
corpus<-corpus[-has.more.than.1] #separate them from main corpus for now
x<-(sapply(gregexpr('\t',multiples),length)/2)-1
for(i in 1:length(x)){
current.additions<-vector() #make empty vector
for(inner.loop in 1:x[i]){
current.additions<-c(current.additions,multiples[i])
}
multiples<-c(multiples, current.additions)
}
multiples<-sort(multiples) #for my benefit
#corpus<-c(corpus,multiples) #if we were done

So the vector 'multiples' now contains the duplicated lines. The original corpus[2] is in there twice, and corpus[3] three time as we want. We'll keep these separate for now. I believe producing duplicated lines uniquely tabbed will require another nested loop: an outer loop for each unique(multiples), another for each occurrence of the node in the line. Within this loop, I've tried pasting regular expressions to the node but haven't produced successful results. I've tried deleting the tabs one-by-one and I've tried removing them all and adding new ones one-by-one, but again with no luck.

This is less something I actually need to do than it is an annoying problem I can't solve. I think I have a good grasp of regular expressions, but this is extremely complicated. Can anybody help in any shape or form?

Incidentally (if it helps), these lines will tab only the first and last occurrence by exploiting greedy and non-greedy matching, but this is of limited value when there are three or more occurrences:
x<-'the life of the party'
x<-gsub('(.*?)(\\bthe\\b)(.*)','\\1\t\\2\t\\3',x) #tabs first one

x<-'the life of the party' #reset
x<-gsub('(.*)(\\bthe\\b)(.*)','\\1\t\\2\t\\3',x) #tabs last one

Any help much appreciated.


--
Kevin Parent, Ph.D
Korea Maritime University
